result.topic_en: Prime divisors of sums of two fourth powers (all of the form 8q+1), a table of such sums factored, and conjectures on when 2 is a biquadratic residue (divisors of the form 64pp+qq) and on q being a biquadratic residue modulo 4q+1.
result.transcription:
Tractatus de numerorum doctrina Cap. 12. 57

455. Contra autem, nulla dabitur duorum biquadratorum summa, quae esset divisibilis per ullum numerum primum hujus seriei 5, 13, 29, 37, 53, 61, 101, etc.; multo vero minus per ullum numerum primum formae $4q-1$, quia ne summa duorum quidem quadratorum per talem numerum est divisibilis.

456. Summa ergo duorum biquadratorum inter se primorum, praeter binarium, alios divisores habere nequit, nisi qui contineantur in forma $8q+1$, ita est:

$1+2^4=17$ $2^4+3^4=97$ $4^4+5^4=881$ $7^4+8^4=73.89$
$1+3^4=2.41$ $2^4+5^4=641$ $4^4+7^4=2657$ $7^4+9^4=2.4481$
$1+4^4=257$ $2^4+7^4=2417$ $4^4+9^4=17.401$ $7^4+10^4=12401$
$1+5^4=2.313$ $2^4+9^4=6577$ $5^4+6^4=17.113$ $8^4+9^4=10657$
$1+6^4=1297$ $3^4+4^4=337$ $5^4+7^4=2.17.89$ $9^4+10^4=16511$.
$1+7^4=2.1201$ $3^4+5^4=2.353$ $5^4+8^4=4721$
$1+8^4=17.241$ $3^4+7^4=2.17.73$ $5^4+9^4=2.3593$
$1+9^4=2.17.193$ $3^4+8^4=4177$ $6^4+7^4=3697$
$1+10^4=73.137$ $3^4+10^4=2.17.593$

457. Si jam quaeratur, quibus divisoribus binarius in residuis reperiatur, id quidem in casibus evolutis § 424 nusquam evenit. At ubi 2 occurrit, ibi etiam $2\alpha$ occurrit; ideoque divisor $4q+1$ factor esse debet talis numeri $a^4-2b^4$, seu $2b^4-a^4$; unde concluduntur hi divisores:

73, 89, 113, 233, 281, 353, 593, 617, 937, 1249, 1889, 2273, 2393, 4177,
4721, 4801, 6529, etc.,

qui numeri in forma $64pp+qq$ contenti videntur. (*)

458. Numeri autem in formula $64pp+qq$ contenti sunt:

73, 89, 113, 233, 257, 281, 337, 353, 577, 593, 601, 617, 881, 937, 1033, 1049,
1097, 1153, 1193, 1201, 1249, etc.,

ubi cum omnes praecedentes occurrant, et reliqui quaesito satisfaciant, nihil est, quod de veritate conjecturae dubitemus, et cum omnes hi numeri sint formae $8n+1$, in residuis tam $-2$ quam $+2$ reperietur.

459. Omnes divisores primos formae $4q+1$ usque ad 101 examinando, inter residua semper occurrit numerus $q$, ita ut esset $q^q-1$ divisibile per $4q+1$, quod si generatim esset verum, simul inter residua forent numeri $q$, $q^2$, $q^3$, $16q$, $81q$, $256q$, $16qq$, $81qq$, hincque $-4$, $q-20$, $-64$, $-4q$.

460. Haec observatio per supra § 389 allatam confirmatur, ubi animadvertimus numerum 2 inter residua quadratorum esse, si divisor primus sit formae $8p+1$, esse autem non-residuum,

(*) Script. ad marg. Ut 3 sit residuum, divisor esse debet $pp+qq$, ut sit vel $p=12m$, vel $p=3(2m+1)$ et $q=4n+2$. Ut 5 sit residuum, divisor fit $=100pp+qq$.

L. Euleri Op. postuma. T. I. 8

methods.what: Sums of two fourth powers have no prime divisors of the form 4q-1 nor primes 5,13,29,... (≡5 mod 8)
methods.quote: nulla dabitur duorum biquadratorum summa, quae esset divisibilis per ullum numerum primum hujus seriei 5, 13, 29, 37, 53, 61, 101, etc.; multo vero minus per ullum numerum primum formae $4q-1$

methods.what: Odd prime divisors of a^4+b^4 (coprime) are ≡1 mod 8
methods.quote: Summa ergo duorum biquadratorum inter se primorum, praeter binarium, alios divisores habere nequit, nisi qui contineantur in forma $8q+1$

methods.what: Table of factorizations of a^4+b^4 for small a,b
If 2 is a biquadratic residue mod p then p divides a^4-2b^4; list of such primes
methods.quote: divisor $4q+1$ factor esse debet talis numeri $a^4-2b^4$, seu $2b^4-a^4$

methods.what: Empirical list of primes of the form 64p^2+q^2
methods.quote: Numeri autem in formula $64pp+qq$ contenti sunt:

items.quote: qui numeri in forma $64pp+qq$ contenti videntur.
items.english: which numbers seem to be contained in the form 64pp+qq.

items.quote: nihil est, quod de veritate conjecturae dubitemus, et cum omnes hi numeri sint formae $8n+1$, in residuis tam $-2$ quam $+2$ reperietur.
items.english: there is no reason to doubt the truth of the conjecture, and since all these numbers are of the form 8n+1, both -2 and +2 will be found among the residues.

items.quote: Omnes divisores primos formae $4q+1$ usque ad 101 examinando, inter residua semper occurrit numerus $q$, ita ut esset $q^q-1$ divisibile per $4q+1$, quod si generatim esset verum
items.english: Examining all prime divisors of the form 4q+1 up to 101, the number q always occurs among the residues, so that q^q-1 is divisible by 4q+1; if this were true in general...

items.quote: Ut 3 sit residuum, divisor esse debet $pp+qq$, ut sit vel $p=12m$, vel $p=3(2m+1)$ et $q=4n+2$. Ut 5 sit residuum, divisor fit $=100pp+qq$.
items.english: For 3 to be a residue, the divisor must be pp+qq with either p=12m, or p=3(2m+1) and q=4n+2. For 5 to be a residue, the divisor becomes 100pp+qq.
